problem: The parenthetical '(0 to 23 in 24-hour mode, set by setIs24HourView(true))' suggests getHour() changes range when the picker is in 12-hour display mode. A student can read this as 'getHour() returns 1 to 12 in 12-hour mode', which is wrong.
fix: Write: 'getHour() always returns 0 to 23; setIs24HourView(true) only changes what the widget shows (whether the AM/PM column appears), not the value getHour() returns. getMinute() returns 0 to 59.'

problem: 'id is the row id the adapter reports (for an ArrayAdapter it equals position)' is true only while the ListView has no header or footer. Once addHeaderView is used the ListView's adapter is the header-wrapping adapter, ids come from the inner ArrayAdapter, and id no longer equals position (header rows report -1).
fix: Write: 'id is the row id the adapter reports; for a plain ArrayAdapter it equals position only when no header or footer has been added. With a header, position is offset by the header count while id stays the ArrayAdapter index.'

problem: It says position 'shifts the moment a header or footer view is added'. A footer does not shift any existing row's position; it only adds a row after the last item.
fix: Write: 'A header shifts every data row by the number of headers added (so Pear moves from 2 to 3); a footer adds a row at the end and shifts nothing.'

problem: Saying the DatePicker 'is set with init(year, month, day, listener)' without saying when the listener fires leaves a gap next to the Spinner point about setSelection. Students then expect init to call the listener, and do not know how to change the date from code.
fix: Add: 'init(...) sets the starting date and registers OnDateChangedListener, which fires only when the user changes the date, not during init. To move the date from code, call updateDate(year, month, day); read it with getYear(), getMonth(), getDayOfMonth().'

problem: 'getSelectedItemPosition() returns the index' leaves out the empty case, which matters because the same section already quotes -1 for RadioGroup.
fix: Write: 'getSelectedItemPosition() returns the index of the current choice, or -1 (INVALID_POSITION) when there is no adapter or nothing is selected; getSelectedItem() returns the object at that index.'
